original_value: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is an effective tool for subsurface detection. Due to the influence of the environment and equipment, the echoes of GPR contain significant noise. In order to suppress noise for GPR data, a method based on singular value decomposition (SVD) of a window-length-optimized Hankel matrix is proposed in this paper. First, SVD is applied to decompose the Hankel matrix of the original data, and the fourth root of the fourth central moment of singular values is used to optimize the window length of the Hankel matrix. Then, the difference spectrum of singular values is used to construct a threshold, which is used to distinguish between components of effective signals and components of noise. Finally, the Hankel matrix is reconstructed with singular values corresponding to effective signals to suppress noise, and the denoised data are recovered from the reconstructed Hankel matrix. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified with both synthetic and field measurements. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve noise removal performance under different detection scenarios.

result.paraphrase: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a useful means of subsurface detection, but its echoes are heavily affected by environmental and equipment-related noise. To suppress noise in GPR data, this paper proposes a method that applies singular value decomposition (SVD) to a Hankel matrix with optimized window length. First, SVD is used to decompose the Hankel matrix formed from the original data, and the window length is optimized using the fourth root of the fourth central moment of the singular values. Next, a threshold is built from the singular-value difference spectrum to separate effective signal components from noise components. Finally, the Hankel matrix is reconstructed using the singular values associated with effective signals, and the denoised data are recovered from the reconstructed matrix. The proposed approach is validated using both synthetic and field measurements, and the results indicate that it can improve noise removal performance across different detection scenarios.
